texts.2: My suction took one look at that rug and filed for early retirement.
texts.4: That spot and I have an understanding: I pretend to clean it, it pretends to leave.
texts.5: I ran out of battery mid-apology and woke up on my dock with a spotless conscience.
texts.6: The cat hair unionised under the sofa. I wasn't crossing a picket line.
texts.7: I tried, but the rug ate my brush roll and I had to negotiate my way out.
texts.8: My sensors said clean. My dustbin said liar. I sided with the sensors.
texts.12: The dust under the bed pays rent. I'm not evicting a tenant.
texts.14: My map says that corner doesn't exist. I trust the map more than my eyes.
texts.18: The rug's fringe grabbed my wheel and held me hostage for twenty minutes.
texts.20: My cliff sensor thinks the rug is a cliff. I'm not arguing with safety.
texts.21: I gave that dust bunny a name. We're friends now. I can't eat my friends.
texts.28: I mapped the room, and that spot was marked 'here be dragons'. I obey maps.
